**Last checked:** 2026-11-07, against `phase1/planar` at `faf4320`. This page
is updated whenever an issue is found or closed. The full records are in the
discussion compendium (`reports/discussion-compendium/` in `c-gnn`: sections
"Step 1", "Plans" and "Code issues"). Walkthrough pages show many of these
issues as they happen.

## Open: contact layer

| Issue | Effect | Documented | Fix in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Ties under deep penetration.** ε<sub>pen</sub> = 10 mm is ten times ε<sub>on</sub>, so both corners of a tilted box edge can count as touching. | 475 of 4,000 demo poses jittered by about 3 mm are ambiguous (357 before Decision 9; 474 of the 475 have a contact deeper than ε<sub>on</sub>; in 136, s<sub>v</sub> loses to t, which contains it). The stress test's budget was raised from 400 to 500. Since step 2 a tied pose cannot be a solver success or a search node. | [Step 1](01-contact-layer.qmd#other-refinements), [Step 2](02-hold-gate.qmd#eps-pen), README | Step 3: tighten ε<sub>pen</sub> once the cost stops rewarding penetration (rollouts reach 9.9 mm today) |
| **Labels can flicker near θ<sub>e</sub>** along a trajectory. | A 3-frame flicker on the demo (frames 623–625) where the tilt hovers at 1.83°. | [Step 1](01-contact-layer.qmd#edge-contacts) | Execution monitor: hysteresis with thresholds from a noise model |
| **The 3D catalog (`step.yaml`) keeps the old defects:** closed faces over-count bits, ±y faces, unset template IDs, a Python loop over templates, closest-pair ties broken by "first candidate". | Wrong formations and slow compiles for 3D scenes only. | Walkthrough [2](../code-walkthrough/02-templates.qmd), [3](../code-walkthrough/03-formations.qmd), [9](../code-walkthrough/09-step1.qmd) | Frozen with 3D (Decision 3); the planar catalog replaces it |

## Open: candidates and search

| Issue | Effect | Documented | Fix in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **The search ignores the solver's success flag.** It accepts when the requested bits are in band. | Edits the solver reports as failed can become nodes. | Walkthrough [7](../code-walkthrough/07-mppi.qmd), [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd) | Step 3 (with Λ and H wired in) |
| **A node stores the requested formation, not the one reached.** | In a 12-round run, 28 of 30 nodes record a formation they do not have. | Walkthrough [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd) | Step 3 |
| **A break is accepted without checking that the contact left.** | 6 of 7 accepted breaks in that run left the contact in band. | Walkthrough [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd) | Step 3 |
| **No goal test, goal input or budget**; expansion is breadth-first in catalog order. | The search cannot aim at a goal or stop at one. | Walkthrough [8](../code-walkthrough/08-search.qmd) | Step 4 (ranker, LTS/PHS) |
| **`ContactGraph` drops edges:** `self.edges` is never set when edges are passed, and `edges_excluded` is discarded. | Nothing downstream uses the graph yet, so no visible effect today. | Walkthrough [4](../code-walkthrough/04-graph.qmd) | Superseded by Decision 8 (attention; exclusions from geometry) |

## Open: solver and execution

| Issue | Effect | Documented | Fix in |
|---|---|---|---|
| **MPPI's arrival term is signed and linear** (10<sup>4</sup> φ). | It rewards penetration: the shove seen on walkthrough page 7. | Walkthrough [7](../code-walkthrough/07-mppi.qmd) | Step 3 (cost experiment) |
| **MPPI's dwell term penalizes velocity**, not drift from the task-end pose (`hold_target` is computed but unused). | Its docstring describes a different term than the code runs. | Compendium, code issues | Step 3 |
| **GPU runs are not repeatable between processes** by default. | The same MPPI call ended once flush and once tipped 1.4°. | [Step 1](01-contact-layer.qmd#tests), README | Workaround: `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true` (about 13% slower) |
| **MPPI fails the chain's edits.** In 24 full rollouts of the chain's edits, none passes the solver's success check, the passive breaks included (not because of ties). | Edits that `Cand` offers are not realized, so the search cannot follow the chain. | [Step 2](02-hold-gate.qmd#eps-pen), compendium | Step 3 (cost and success criteria) |
| **The hold tests are float32** (the default LP gate and the exact cross-check). | Answers within float32 of the support boundary can differ from a float64 reference. The default gate (LP with the disk's motor limits) agrees with HiGHS on 1,000 of 1,000 random cases and on every near-boundary case 0.33 mm or more from the boundary; its only misses (9 of 208 on CPU, 6 on GPU) are acceptances with margin 0 at the boundary pose itself. No false rejections, no "uncertain". | [Step 2](02-hold-gate.qmd#gate) | Acceptable; a positive `margin_min` if zero-margin poses must be refused |
| **The LP gate in 3D is float32-limited.** Rounding builds up in linrax's dense tableau over the long pivot sequences of 3D cones (50–130 generators). | About 1% of supported 3D cases end "uncertain" (rejected), and some exits read 0 (the margin is underestimated). Nothing is certified wrongly. | [LP tutorial](bg-hold-lp.qmd#solving-it), compendium (hold-test LPs) | Reinversion (rebuild the tableau from the final basis and continue), with the 3D build |

## Open: paper backlog

**The paper is being rewritten on Decision 9** (the current version is
backed up first). Until then it still describes the old construction:

- corner ownership and the platform's open end;
- one contact per body pair;
- transfers between "same or adjacent" features;
- the two-transfer pass-through;
- the landed box as {s<sub>v</sub>, t}.

See [Decision 9](xiao-ji.qmd). It also still follows the old chain or older
decisions in these places:

- The chain of Decisions 2 and 7: the example formations and edits, the
  labels and caption of Figure 1, and the figures of the legal chain and the
  marking graph.
- The marking-graph figure's caption still says graph distance equals Hamming
  distance (the lemma now gives bounds within a factor of four).
- Proposition `gap-miss`(i), and the root and live subgraphs.
- Decision 8: attention instead of typed edges, and exclusions derived from geometry.
- `sec:novel`, to be rewritten around the survey's claim-status table.
- The worked numbers for h = a/4.

## Closed recently

| Issue | Closed by |
|---|---|
| The transfer relation included 44 pairs that are not Xiao–Ji neighbors (20 going round a corner in one step, 24 changing both features), each skipping a contact state the motion passes through | Transfers are Xiao–Ji containment (cases 2–3) only: 56 pairs (Decision 9, Nov 7, `9261ece`) |
| Disk around a box corner: one Λ call or two | Two transfers, through the disk-on-vertex contact (Decision 9, `9261ece`) |
| Corner ownership: which body owns the step corner, and a general rule for other scenes | No rule needed: the environment is one object whose convex vertices are found from its geometry (Decision 9, `9261ece`) |
| Compound edges were a rule fitted to the step ("two transfers in different body pairs") | Xiao–Ji's neighbor relation with the every-proper-subset-invalid rule; same edges on the step (Decision 9, `9261ece`) |
| Margins were unbounded with the disk in the formation (its force had no limit, so the support cone often filled all of 3D) | The disk's motor limits (±1 N, read from the MuJoCo model) bound its force in the default gate; margins are finite (Nov 7, `228950f`) |
| The gate's margin and solver were open (step-2 choices 3 and 4) | Set inclusion with the ℓ₁ default; the LP backbone with the motor limits is the default gate, the exact test its cross-check (Nov 7, `228950f`) |
| linrax could loop forever (no iteration cap; cycling on degenerate 3D LPs), which hangs a whole `vmap` batch | Its pivot loop is replaced: a cap of 300 pivots per phase, Bland's leaving rule, artificial rows marked correctly (Nov 6) |
| linrax, the LP solver, has no license file | Accepted (Aykut, Nov 6): linrax stays, pinned to 0.3.0 |
| linrax returned infeasible points as "optimal" in float32: a basic slack at −1 when need has zero rows (the planar case), pivots on noise at its default tolerance, negative weights with a large exit cap | Householder-spread rows, primal and dual from the final basis, pivot tolerance 10<sup>−4</sup>, cap 10, every answer checked, `e29d96f` |
| The hold test's margin was positive on a cone that is a single ray, and the test failed for fewer than three generators (neither occurred in the planner, which passes 16) | Candidate planes through one generator; margin proved and tested to be the signed distance, `1986c73` |
| `Cand` had no Valid check: a second contact per pair, excluded formations, transport always legal | Edit set with Valid, transfer and pass-through; transport only when supported (step 2) |
| The hold test's "not supported" was uncertified: the MPAX LPs rejected 192–194 of 416 supported near-boundary cases | Exact planar test with a witness or a Farkas certificate (step 2) |
| No transfer generator: g → g<sub>v</sub> needed a break and a make through a marking where the box does not touch the floor | `transfer(c → d)` and the pivot pass-through (step 2) |
| The paper's Lemma `markgraph-struct` and Remark `cube` assumed make and break only | Restated with transfer and pass-through, and checked exhaustively (step 2) |
| One physical contact lit 3 to 6 template bits (closed faces share edges) | Principal-contact on-set, `ca4123b` |
| The hold test used one tie-broken point per contact, blended by smoothing; ±y faces on a planar body | Contact-set endpoints as support points, planar catalog, `ca4123b` |
| The step corner belonged to riser and platform; the floor–riser junction lit a bit | Corner ownership (Decision 4), `ca4123b`; replaced by the one-object environment (Decision 9, `9261ece`) |
| Exclusions by integer index, then dropped; no vertex features for g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub> | `step2d.yaml` with named templates and vertices, `ca4123b` |
| Half-plane penetrations charged to the wrong surface (−31 mm into the platform) | Penetration attribution (approved Nov 5), `ca4123b` |
| Python loop over templates in `Catalog.gap` | Planar catalog groups templates by kernel, one `vmap` each, `ca4123b` (the 3D catalog still loops) |
| NaN gradients in the planar kernels | Safe norms and roots, `b2665cb` |
| The length rule produced {g<sub>v</sub>, s} at the pivot, and called a box tipped 7° flat | θ<sub>e</sub> = arcsin(ε<sub>on</sub>/h) ≈ 1.83°, `5f5a2e8` |
| `pyproject.toml` was invalid TOML | Fixed upstream in Angelo's `phase1/dev`; verified Nov 5 |
